It supersedes the previous report (which audited arena/01a0c952-newjollof at 5855dfd). 17 files differ; everything unchanged in this branch inherits its verified findings from the prior audit and was re-executed where possible to confirm.

BRANCH RE-AUDIT What the support modules fixed, and what they didn’t

The desk is real. The money still isn’t.

This branch replaces two fake promises — filing disputes and contacting support — with genuinely working, database-backed modules: five live-chat queues, an agent console, and a dispute centre with claims, statuses and decisions. That is real progress. But it also introduces two new severe flaws — a chat-close endpoint that lets strangers read and end other people’s conversations, and an agent form that hands out platform-admin rights — while leaving the entire paid-booking core (payments, gift cards, calendar enforcement, suspensions) exactly as broken as before.

See the 10 critical findings All 92 capabilities
THE BOTTOM LINE

Support now works.
Commerce still can’t be trusted.

Live chat and disputes are usable features with fixable edge cases — except the two P0 security holes. Bookings, payments and refunds remain confirmation theatre. Neither module is ready for real customers together with the unchanged core.

Same isolation rules as before: no real money, email or production access; synthetic accounts only.

01 / Reading the results

How to read this re-audit.

Same three classes as before, plus a new distinction this branch forces: a feature can be genuinely implemented yet unsafe to ship. “Partially functional” below often means “works until you poke the edges.”

Fully operational/functional

The named operation works.

Verified against this branch where the code is shared; carried from the prior audit where files are byte-identical (marked “reconfirmed”).

None of the new support modules earn this yet — their cores work but each has an unresolved flaw.

Partially functional

Real implementation, incomplete guarantees.

The dispute centre and chat desk live here: the features exist, persist and behave — with privacy, scoping, draft or money gaps that block launch trust.

New this branch: F87–F92 all sit here or below; none is vaporware.

Not working at all

The named outcome doesn’t happen.

Payments, gift-card trust, suspensions, exports-to-nowhere controls — re-executed on this branch and unchanged.

Carried rows note their original evidence IDs; all were re-run here except where stated.

Reconfirmed vs. inherited.

Because the two branches share most files, this audit re-ran the complete API suite (98 checks) and the browser suite against the new snapshot; results matched the prior audit line-for-line on unchanged code. Rows whose files are byte-identical between branches (SEO, sitemap, installer base flow) cite the prior run and say so.

A record is not an action — now literally.

The dispute centre proves the rule in both directions: writing a timeline event and a “refunded” payments row is real record-keeping; it still isn’t money moving. Same with “sent” emails on disabled transport, “connected” channel flags, and “saved” drafts that a repaint discards.

03 / Critical findings

Ten things to understand first.

Two are new on this branch (chat privacy, privilege escalation); the rest are the carried core problems, reconfirmed verbatim on the new code. Every example is from isolated synthetic tests.

Do not open the chat desk or dispute centre to real staff or claimants yet. P0 = fix/contain before any live use; P1 = complete before depending on it; P2 = later/optional; the carried findings from the previous audit retain their priorities.

01Visitor privacy
P0

Anyone who knows a chat reference can close that chat and read the whole transcript.

no ownership checkon the visitor close path (C21/C41)

post/poll/rate all verify the visitor token, but close does not: the API takes the ref, closes the session, and returns the bundle — which includes every message — to whoever asked. A guessed or leaked ref is enough to end someone else’s support chat and read it.

Evidence, impact & what must change

What established this finding

A synthetic stranger closed an active chat with a wrong token (C21) and received 3 private messages (C41).

Why it matters

Private customer conversations, which may include booking and payment details, are exposed by a single unauthenticated POST.

Recommended response

Require the visitor token (or the signed-in owner/supervisor) on close, exactly as poll/post/rate do; never return the transcript from close.

What a trustworthy outcome looks like

Closing with a foreign ref returns 403 and zero messages; legitimate visitors and their agents still close normally.

Related capability assessments
F87
02Privilege escalation
P0

Creating a chat agent with a temporary password grants platform admin.

role=adminregardless of the chosen agent role (C32)

saveAgent’s “create an account for this agent” path writes role=admin for both existing matched users and new accounts. A supervisor adding a front-line agent with a password therefore mints a full administrator who can export all users (C33), and pausing the agent doesn’t take that away (C34).

Evidence, impact & what must change

What established this finding

Created agent “agent-one” role in chat_agents but the linked user row became admin; the same account then downloaded the users CSV.

Why it matters

A support-administration convenience becomes a total platform-compromise path.

Recommended response

Never set roles or create user accounts from saveAgent. Provision staff through an explicit, separately-authorized admin action, and invalidate sessions when staff are paused.

What a trustworthy outcome looks like

Password provisioning creates at most a guest-level account; role changes are their own audited operation; pausing revokes live console access.

Related capability assessments

03Money truth
P0

Dispute refunds are bookkeeping, and the bookkeeping can double-count.

gateway “dispute”refund rows with no provider movement (D19/D20)

The decision flow writes payments rows, flips escrow labels, flags fraud and emails claimants — impressive wiring, but no gateway is contacted. Worse, a second decision can add more refund rows past the booking total (D31), a full refund can leave the booking row pending while escrow flips to refunded (D30), a “no action” outcome still stores the typed refund (D34), and re-deciding a closed case throws 500 after already mutating the dispute (D24).

Evidence, impact & what must change

What established this finding

A £-scale synthetic case: refund ≤ total enforced, totals exceeded on repeat, repeated decide returned 500 mid-write.

Why it matters

Finance cannot trust dispute outcomes; claimants may be promised refunds nobody issued; a crashed write leaves half-states.

Recommended response

Route outcomes through a real settlement/refund pipeline (or label decisions record-only), enforce one reconciled total per booking, wrap decision+event+flag+ledger in one transaction with an idempotency key.

What a trustworthy outcome looks like

A decision either executes verifiable money movement or is explicitly marked “recorded, not paid”; totals never exceed the booking; retries are idempotent.

06Staff tooling
P1

Canned replies leak across agents and ignore their own off switch.

is_active ignoredin the use path (C38); scope ignored (C39)

Saving supports scope/personal/active flags, but allCanned and use-canned read every row: a supervisor’s disabled reply can be sent by any agent, and a personal reply shows up in someone else’s picker.

Evidence, impact & what must change

What established this finding

C38 sent a disabled reply through another agent; C39 saw a personal reply.

Why it matters

Message integrity for visitors and agent trust in their saved snippets both break.

Recommended response

Filter both listing and use by is_active and scope; add a regression test per scope.

What a trustworthy outcome looks like

A disabled reply is neither listed nor usable; personal replies never appear for others.

Related capability assessments
F88
07Workflow polish
P1

Support drafts evaporate: the 4s/6s refresh overwrites the composer.

draft=""after one poll cycle (U04/U07)

Both widget and console full-repaint the panel on their interval. Any half-typed message — often the longest, most considered text in support work — is gone before the agent or visitor presses send.

Evidence, impact & what must change

What established this finding

U04 and U07 filled the composer, waited one cycle, found it empty.

Why it matters

Support agents retype; visitors abandon mid-thought. This is a daily-quality killer for a live-chat product.

Recommended response

Update the message list in place (append/patch) and leave the composer untouched; or snapshot/restore the textarea around repaints.

What a trustworthy outcome looks like

Type during three poll cycles; the draft persists; sending works immediately after.

Related capability assessments

08Dispute details
P1

Case-file edges mislabel, mis-render and strand claimants.

U19/D10/D32broken reopen, javascript: evidence links, tokenless share link, public case list

“Reopen (decision stands)” sends status=resolved — invalid from resolved — so reopening silently fails (U19). Evidence links are rendered as anchors without scheme checks (D10). The anonymous claimant’s only recovery path is a link whose token lives only in the filing browser’s localStorage (U22). Host can withdraw a guest’s case (D17); a withdrawn case can still be decided (D18). And the public dispute-categories endpoint embeds a recent-case list with claimant subject and reference, readable without signing in (D32).

Evidence, impact & what must change

What established this finding

All six reproduced in browser/API tests.

Why it matters

Mediators record wrong outcomes; anonymous claimants are stranded; anchor hrefs are an XSS-class vector; case existence leaks publicly.

Recommended response

Fix the reopen payload; validate/sanitize attachment URLs (http(s) only, rel=noopener already present); email the token with the reference; tighten role rules; strip the recent-case list from the public stats.

What a trustworthy outcome looks like

Each action does what its label says, unsafe links are rejected, an anonymous claimant with only the emailed link can reopen the case, and anonymous stats contain no case data.

Related capability assessments
F89F90
09Deploy tooling
P1

Migration double-run duplicates seeds on the development dialect.

8→16dispute categories on second run (T06)

The runner promises safe repetition and repairs missing unique keys — but on SQLite the translator strips the table-level UNIQUE keys, and ensure_unique_index issues MySQL-only ALTER syntax, so the repair no-ops and every seed doubles. On MySQL the inline keys make INSERT IGNORE behave; that path couldn’t be exercised here.

Evidence, impact & what must change

What established this finding

T06 after restoring the six unique indexes by hand showed the intended behaviour; the runner alone could not.

Why it matters

Duplicate queues/categories/replies appear in every picker; operators get a green result page.

Recommended response

Make repair dialect-aware (CREATE UNIQUE INDEX on SQLite; verify after), gate seeds with NOT EXISTS like the other inserts, and add double-run assertions to the release checklist.

What a trustworthy outcome looks like

Run twice on both dialects: counts stay 8/5/7/1 and the result page reports per-table counts.

Related capability assessments

config unchangedtracked config blob byte-identical to the previous audit

includes/config.php (non-placeholder DB password/app key), the private wal7zkit dump and public_html.zip remain at the web root with no .htaccess. This branch also adds install/diagnose|why|migrate to that same public tree — useful tools whose extended admin sections leak environment detail if the folder is web-exposed.

Evidence, impact & what must change

What established this finding

git diff of the config blob against the audited base is empty; files tracked in the repo.

Why it matters

Any public copy of this checkout — plus the new diagnostic endpoints — widens the exposure the first audit flagged.

Recommended response

Rotate secrets, move config out of the repo, remove/protect dumps, and deny install/ in deployment (the guide already warns about never overwriting config).

What a trustworthy outcome looks like

Fresh clone contains no live credentials; diagnostics unreachable or admin-network-restricted on the deployed host.

F01Discovery & contentWebsite shell, ordinary navigation, mobile menu and theme Fully operational/functionalMaintain

The website’s basic frame works. This is a genuine working part of the product, but a working menu does not prove that everything behind its links works.

What this feature should do

Help visitors move around the website, open the navigation on a phone, and choose a comfortable reading theme.

Why this matters to the business or user

Guests can navigate and return to familiar sections. Preserve this foundation while repairing the business workflows underneath it.

What the audit actually found

Header/footer navigation and mobile drawer work; light/dark preference survives reload. This is the navigation shell, not a certification of every destination or accessibility.

Recommended next step

Retain regression coverage for signed-in and mobile navigation.

Recommended acceptance checks

  1. Check navigation, sign-in/sign-out links and the mobile drawer in both signed-in and signed-out states.
  2. Switch themes, refresh and verify that the preference remains without obscuring controls.

F03Discovery & contentStay search and filtering Partially functionalP1

Some filters narrow the list, but the search is not reliable enough to promise an available home in the exact neighbourhood requested.

What this feature should do

Return homes that actually match a guest’s location, dates, party size, budget and other selected criteria.

Why this matters to the business or user

Guests can waste time on homes outside the intended area or on dates that cannot be reserved. This can reduce trust before checkout even starts.

What the audit actually found

Basic city/capacity/type/price filters exist. Choosing Ikoyi also matches every Lagos residence because the predicate ORs area with city. Dates and flexible-date availability do not filter results; category tabs raise a missing-element error.

Recommended next step

Use explicit city/area identifiers and authoritative date availability; fix tab handlers.

Recommended acceptance checks

  1. An Ikoyi-only search must exclude homes elsewhere in Lagos.
  2. A booked or host-blocked date must affect results, and changing a category must not cause a JavaScript error.

F06Discovery & contentResidence detail pages Partially functionalP1

Some existing homes display correctly, while homes without review scores can look like they do not exist. Publishing a listing is therefore not enough to make it usable.

What this feature should do

Give every published residence a usable detail page, including newly added homes that do not yet have reviews.

F87Live support & disputesLive-chat visitor widget and queues NEW ON THIS BRANCHPartially functionalP0

This branch replaced the “message the concierge” button with a genuine support desk: queues, waiting position, typing indicator, private resume token, closing and rating all really work. Two things keep it from being fully operational: the periodic refresh wipes whatever you had typed but not sent, and—more seriously—the close action checks nobody, so anyone holding a chat reference (even without the token) can close a stranger’s chat and receive their whole transcript back.

What this feature should do

Let any visitor reach a human: pick a topic, start a conversation, exchange messages with a live agent, resume later, end and rate the chat.

Why this matters to the business or user

Support conversations now work in production, but an attacker or careless link-share can read or close other people’s chats, and agents/visitors lose drafted replies when a poll repaints underneath them.

What the audit actually found

A real two-way support channel now exists: visitors pick one of five seeded queues, start a session that queues correctly, exchange escaped messages with the assigned agent, see queue position and typing indicators, resume the same chat after reload through a browser-stored private token, end the chat into the rate state, and everything is capped, throttled and CSRF-guarded. Unsent drafts are wiped by the 4-second poll re-render (U04), the visitor close endpoint performs no ownership check and hands the entire transcript back to any caller holding the ref (C21/C41 — private text leaked to a stranger), typing beacons and satisfaction ratings skip their ownership/closed-state rules (C14/C15), and there are no attachments, media or translation despite marketing copy elsewhere.

Recommended next step

Require the visitor token/ownership on close exactly as post/rate do and return no transcript to strangers; persist drafts across re-renders; keep capability claims honest until attachments/media/translation exist.

Recommended acceptance checks

  1. Posting/polling/closing/rating all require ownership; a foreign ref+no-token close returns 403 and no messages.
  2. Type a draft, wait through two poll cycles, and confirm the text is still in the box; refresh and confirm resume reuses the same session.
  3. Start from the floating button on a 390px viewport and verify queue choice, first message, agent reply and rating all persist in the database.

What this feature should do

07 / Plain-English glossary

Terms, made useful.

Expanded for this branch: polling, transitions, seeds, idempotency keys, privilege escalation and reserved words.

No matching terms. Try a shorter search.

API
The interface through which the browser or a mobile app asks the server to do something. A button may call an API—or may simply display a popup without calling anything.
Backend / server
The code that applies business rules, reads and writes the database, and talks to external providers. Critical pricing, permissions and payment decisions must be enforced here.
Frontend / browser state
The screen and JavaScript running in the user’s browser. Its local copy of data can become stale even if a database update succeeded.
Status flag
A stored word or number such as paid, verified or connected. A flag describes a claimed state; it is not independent proof that a charge, verification or connection occurred.
Toast / success popup
A short on-screen message. In this audit, several buttons only show such a message and do not perform the service the message announces.
CRUD
Create, Read, Update and Delete—the basic record-management operations. Working CRUD is valuable, but creating an invitation row does not send or accept an invitation.
Database schema
The definitions of tables and fields. Code that writes read_at will fail if the delivered table only has read_flag.
Response contract / JSON envelope
The agreed shape of an API response. If the server sends {state: ...} and the browser reads {data: ...}, both pieces can run while the screen never receives the new state.
Authentication
Proving who someone is, usually by validating credentials. It differs from deciding which actions that person may perform.
Authorization
Checking whether the authenticated person is allowed to perform a particular action on a particular record. A guest knowing a booking reference must not be enough to approve a host’s request.
Ownership check
A specific authorization rule tying a booking, conversation, listing or report to the permitted guest/owner. Web and mobile must enforce equivalent rules.
CSRF protection
A defense against another website causing unintended actions through a person’s signed-in browser. A valid CSRF check does not replace permission or business-rule validation.
MFA / 2FA / OTP
Multi-factor or two-factor authentication adds a distinct proof beyond the password. OTP means one-time password/code. A shared static configured code is not a complete enrolled authenticator system.
Session / bearer token
A credential used after sign-in. A website commonly uses a session cookie; mobile commonly sends a bearer token. Suspension or compromise may require revoking both.
KYC / verification
Know Your Customer or identity-verification work. It needs real evidence and a review/provider outcome—not merely an admin-set flag or a phone number typed into a profile.
Payment gateway
A provider that actually processes a payment. A row labelled initiated is not evidence that the provider collected money.
Webhook
An event sent by an external service to your server, often to report payment status. It must be authenticated and matched to the correct booking, amount and currency.
Escrow
A real arrangement governing the custody and release of funds under defined conditions. Calling a database field escrow does not create that arrangement or its legal/financial safeguards.
Ledger / reconciliation
A traceable record of money or points movements. Reconciliation checks the record against actual provider events and balances; an ordinary booking total is not a reconciled settlement.
Idempotency / replay safety
Repeating the same operation should have the intended effect only once. This prevents retries from charging twice, spending gift credit twice or reversing a toggle unexpectedly.
Atomic operation
A set of changes that succeeds together or fails together. Gift-card debit and related reservation creation should not leave half-completed financial state.
Race condition / concurrency
Two operations overlap in time. Both can see a room as free before either saves a booking unless the database/service protects the decision. Native-MySQL concurrency was not tested here.
Worker / scheduled job
A process that runs work after an event or at a later time, such as sending check-in instructions or watching waitlist availability. Saving a trigger name does not create that process.
SMTP / email delivery
A protocol used to hand email to a mail server. The audit intentionally disabled email; delivery still needs sandbox testing and honest handling of accepted/rejected responses.
Stored HTML / injection surface
Text from a user or stored record can be interpreted as webpage markup if it is not escaped/safely sanitized. The audit used a harmless marker to demonstrate markup rendering, not a production exploit.
Canonical URL / sitemap
A canonical identifies the preferred URL for a page; a sitemap lists URLs for discovery. Distinct residences should not accidentally identify themselves as the same generic detail URL.
CSV export
A spreadsheet-friendly text file containing rows and columns. A working download proves records can be exported, not that every exported monetary figure is financially correct.
Bounded capability
The exact operation a rating applies to. For example, working newsletter signup means capturing a subscriber, not automatically sending a newsletter campaign.
Fixture / isolated test
A controlled local set of data and accounts used for testing. This review used synthetic users and transactions rather than production accounts or real payments.
PHP-WASM / SQLite / MySQL
The isolated runtime used WebAssembly PHP and a local SQLite translation of the supplied MySQL schema. Source-confirmed logic defects are separated from harness limitations; native MySQL behavior remains to be checked.
Route smoke check
A basic check that a page responds and renders. A payment page can pass this check even when its Pay control does not collect any money.
Accessibility / WCAG / axe
Accessibility concerns whether people with different abilities can use the interface. WCAG is a standard; axe detects some issues automatically. Passing a viewport test or automated scan alone is not a full accessibility certification.
Source revision / repository snapshot
The specific code version reviewed. This report applies to commit 5855dfdfb422c517ba630cb6f4955a368e45e4b3, not to unreviewed changes or a possibly different live deployment.
Production-ready
Ready for real users, real money and operational responsibility. It requires the complete critical journey, external verification and deployment assurance—not a particular number of completed screens.
Polling (live chat)
Repeatedly asking the server for updates, e.g. every 4 seconds. It’s how the widget and agent desk stay fresh; it costs requests and, in this build, re-renders wipe unsent drafts (F87/F88).
State-transition table
A declared list of allowed status changes (submitted→under_review→evidence→resolved…). The dispute centre enforces one on the server; invalid moves are rejected..
Seed data
Pre-filled rows a migration inserts (categories, queues, canned replies). Idempotent seeding means re-running can’t duplicate them—promised here, proven only on MySQL (F91).
Idempotency key
A client-generated key that makes a retried request safe (booking creation uses X-Client-Key). The dispute decision flow has none, which is part of why re-deciding corrupts state (F90).
Privilege escalation
A lesser role obtaining greater rights through an implementation shortcut—here, the agent-password field silently granting platform admin (F88).
MySQL reserved word
A keyword that cannot be used as a bare identifier; `load` is one. The branch fixed four queries (quoted ``AS `load` ``) and added a scanner in diagnose.php, though the scanner itself is heuristic (F92).

08 / Scope & limitations

What this re-audit does — and does not — prove.

Same boundaries as the first report, plus the notes below specific to this branch.

Established within scope

  • Live chat and disputes are real, database-backed implementations — a genuine functional step up from the prior branch, with specific reproducible defects (privacy, scoping, drafts, reopen, money).
  • All core-commerce failures from the prior audit reproduce byte-identically on this snapshot where the code is shared.
  • The migration works on a clean database and is admin-gated; its double-run claim fails on the SQLite dev path and could not be disproved on MySQL here.
  • No application code was modified for this audit.

Needs independent verification

  • MySQL behavior of the migration idempotency repair and the reserved-word scanner (the bug this branch fixes was itself only MySQL-confirmed by its author).
  • Concurrency: two agents claiming, rapid-fire posts, transactional decision writes — untested against native MySQL.
  • Everything previously listed: live deployment, SMTP, gateways, channels, devices, load, full accessibility, compliance claims.

Safety again: no real emails were sent, no payments were attempted, no external service was contacted, and every account/transaction used here is synthetic. The harmless HTML markers prove rendering paths only.

This branch earns its merge; it doesn’t yet earn customers.

Fix the two P0 support flaws and the carried core plan still leads to the same place: one trustworthy booking-and-money journey, honestly labelled, then the growth features.
